regions.title: Foundations
regions.summary: Triads in every key, and what inversion actually means.

gates.title: Triads
gates.objective: Build a major or minor triad on any root.
gates.preview: A triad is three notes: the root, a third and a fifth. The third is what makes it major or minor — everything else in this game is built on hearing that one note move.

gates.title: Triad inversions
gates.objective: Put any chord tone in the bass, on purpose.
gates.preview: An inversion is not a different chord. It is the same chord with a different note underneath, and the bass is what a listener hears first.

regions.title: Seventh Harmony
regions.summary: The four-note chords the whole language is written in.

gates.title: Seventh chords
gates.objective: Build the six common seventh and sixth chords on any root.
gates.preview: Add one more third on top of a triad and you have a seventh chord. The third and the seventh together are what name it: they are the two notes a jazz musician will not leave out.

gates.title: Seventh inversions
gates.objective: Place the third, fifth or seventh in the bass of a four-note chord.

gates.title: ii-V-I
gates.objective: Play a ii-V-I in any key without working it out first.
gates.preview: Most of the standard repertoire is this progression, moved around. Learn it in one key and you have learned one key; learn what it is made of and you have learned twelve.

regions.title: Jazz Voicings
regions.summary: The shapes a pianist actually plays, rather than the ones a textbook prints.

gates.title: Shell voicings
gates.objective: Play root, third and seventh — and leave the fifth out.
gates.preview: In this exercise the fifth is left out so that the root and the two guide tones sit clearly in the left hand. That is a choice about this voicing, not a rule about the chord.

gates.title: Guide tones
gates.objective: Play the third and seventh alone, and hear the chord anyway.
gates.preview: Two notes are enough to say which chord this is. Once you can hear that, the root belongs to whoever is playing the bass.

gates.title: Rootless voicings
gates.objective: Play the left-hand A position: third, fifth or thirteenth, seventh and ninth.
gates.preview: The A position puts the third lowest. The same four notes rotated give you the B position — they are the same chord, and they do not sound the same.

regions.title: Extensions
regions.summary: Ninths and the colour above the seventh.

gates.title: Ninths
gates.objective: Add a ninth to a seventh chord without losing the chord underneath it.
